seo.title: Hotel and guesthouse insurance in Moldova | ING Broker
seo.description: Assess buildings, equipment, guests' belongings, liability and interruption separately. Prepare hospitality documents before comparing insurance conditions.
seo.keywords: hotel insurance Moldova, guesthouse insurance, hotel property insurance, hospitality liability, hotel business interruption

author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
Insurance for a hotel or guesthouse is assessed in components: buildings, equipment, guest activities and potential losses during closure. A room count is not enough. Kitchens, parking, event rooms and technical equipment can change the questions needed for comparison.

This material is for accommodation operators in the Republic of Moldova, including guesthouses with restaurants. It provides a method of preparing information, not a confirmed coverage package. Each component and the possibility of brokering require checking for the actual situation. The insurer determines acceptance and contractual conditions.

Define the activities actually carried out

State whether the property offers accommodation alone or also meals, events, leisure, transport or equipment rental. Identify activities operated by other businesses at the location. A partner-run restaurant should not be presented as automatically having the same contract and interests as the hotel.

Record opening hours and operating periods. A seasonal guesthouse may have intervals when the building is less closely supervised. No tourists does not mean no risk to installations, roofs or stored property. Describe the real position, including unused areas.

Who owns the building and invests in equipment?

The property owner and hotel operator may be different entities. Separate the building, operator-funded improvements and bedroom furniture. Provide relevant use documents so the discussion follows each party's assets and interests rather than only the trading name at the entrance.

For an old or converted building, describe known materials, renovations and installations. Do not assign the latest bedroom renovation date to the entire property. Use documented information and identify what is unknown. A further technical review may be necessary before a proposal.

Room inventories should be verifiable

Group beds, furniture, televisions, air conditioning and other equipment into clear lists. Identify significant differences between standard and specially equipped rooms. An estimated value per room may be insufficient if some property was recently replaced or belongs to somebody else.

Keep available invoices and records. Ask which valuation basis determines the sum insured, meaning the value stated in the contract. Book value is not automatically the cost of restoring a room after damage. The room price charged to a tourist is not the value of its contents either.

Kitchens and laundries have their own machinery

Prepare a simple list of cooking, refrigeration, washing and drying equipment. For important installations, record use, known age and documented maintenance. A kitchen serving a small breakfast should not be described like one continuously preparing meals for large events.

Separate equipment breakdown from damage to food or linen. Ask for each consequence to be checked in the proposed conditions. A building policy does not automatically confirm these losses are paid. Where activity is outsourced, describe property transport and the provider's documented responsibilities.

Guests' belongings are not hotel equipment

Tourists' luggage and personal items have a different owner from bedroom furniture. Ask expressly how related claims are treated. Do not tell guests every item left in a room is insured merely because the hotel has property insurance.

Describe storage facilities, receiving arrangements and records if provided. An initial assessment does not require copies of every guest's identity documents or named reservation lists. Liability needs separate legal review; this article establishes no universal statutory luggage limits.

Visitors, events and civil liability

A person can visit a restaurant or event without staying overnight. Include these flows and spaces used: terraces, stairs, parking, playgrounds and other existing facilities. Do not declare services not offered, but do not omit important occasional activities.

General liability concerns different questions from restoring your own property. Check the activities, people and territory considered in the proposal. Special facilities, such as leisure areas, should be expressly assessed. The label “hotel” does not prove every activity at the address is included.

Seasonality influences continuity planning

Compare busy and quiet periods using financial records that explain them. Interruption before a booked event may have a different economic effect from the same period out of season. Do not invent future revenue to complete a form; use records and clearly marked assumptions.

Any business interruption insurance requires separate reading, including its triggering event and relevant period. Cancelled reservations or lower tourist demand should not automatically be considered insured risks. Do not confuse the hotel's business plan with the obligations of a property policy.

Prepare temporary solutions before a breakdown

Ask the team what can continue if a wing, kitchen or heating installation becomes unusable. Identify alternatives and who can authorise moving services. This plan is operationally useful even if a particular expense is not accepted by insurance. Do not wait for an incident to find technical records.

Separate reinstatement, cleaning and temporary service costs. When reviewing the proposal, request identification of each category in its documents. A list of possible expenses does not confirm insurer payment or replace the approval procedure applicable to a claim.

Compare prices without losing details

A premium is the amount paid for the policy. Keep buildings, property, values and activities consistent across requests. A lower premium based on an incomplete description does not necessarily provide equivalent hotel or guesthouse protection.

An excess or deductible is the portion borne by the insured under the conditions. Read the formula, special limits and exclusions, meaning uncovered situations. Request practical explanations for important property risks. This article supplies no per-room tariff or promised discount for accommodation capacity.

Documents useful for the first discussion

Organise a site description, activities, inventory categories, documented values and known incident history. Add maintenance information and planned changes. Room photographs may help explain space but should not include guests, reservations or screens showing personal information.

Designate technical and financial contacts where the roles differ. Check missing documents together before calling the file complete. A provider may request further information or inspection. The editorial list is not an identical procedure for all hotels and insurers in Moldova.

Example: a guesthouse with a restaurant and event room

A hypothetical guesthouse has bedrooms, a kitchen and an event room used at weekends. The operator separates each space's equipment, checks rented event property and prepares shared installation information. Instead of requesting only “guesthouse insurance”, the operator describes the activities requiring assessment.

Comparison considers own property, third-party claims and possible interruption separately. The example is not a real customer and does not confirm an all-inclusive package. It avoids an overly broad description that leaves the business's most important needs unclear.

What to update at renewal

Check bedroom renovations, restaurant extensions and added services. A new terrace or recently purchased appliances do not automatically appear in last year's inventory. Compare reality with declared information and clarify relevant changes under the contract's conditions.

Keep a dated site record and list of unanswered questions. Do not fill unknowns with optimistic answers just to speed discussion. Written clarification of important property or a service is more useful than assuming the hotel's name already includes it.

Unoccupied periods and outdoor facilities

A property closed in winter may retain furniture, appliances and installations requiring supervision. Describe how rooms are checked and who can respond to a problem. This article is not a technical preservation manual; competent people determine suitable measures for the existing equipment.

Create a separate inventory for grounds, outbuildings, outdoor furniture and other facilities. Distinguish fixed, movable and temporarily supplied items. An overall photograph does not identify every object or confirm its inclusion in an insurance contract.

A rural guesthouse may depend on its own water supply, boiler or other technical equipment. Record their roles and practical alternatives during an outage. Do not assume the source of every interruption lies in the main building or that all consequences can be insured together.

At season-end, compare the property list against what actually remains at each location. Keep important movement records without exposing keys, access codes or unnecessary security details. This record supports a precise discussion and does not replace applicable security and maintenance requirements.

Frequently asked questions about hotels and guesthouses

Does building insurance include tourists' luggage?

Not automatically. Guests' property and related claims need separate assessment from the building and hotel furniture. Request a documented explanation for storage services you provide.

How much does guesthouse insurance cost?

Compare cost against the site description, activities, property, values and conditions. Without these details, a per-room figure is not automatically an appropriate offer for your business.

Are cancelled reservations included?

Do not assume property insurance pays for every cancellation. An economic component, if available, must be checked against contractual events, periods and calculation rules.

Who decides compensation after damage?

The insurer assesses the case under the contract and documents. The broker intermediates and explains steps without replacing that decision or guaranteeing an outcome.
